title: Source Citation to an Image

illustrates.quote: Images. Place any associated source citation or copyright information appearing with an image in a new 7-5 paragraph following the caption. Follow print for wording and sequence of information. (See Sample 9-7: Source Citation to an Image on page 9-18.)

blocks.text: Locomotives (see the Norris above) or horses pulled cars on the levels between inclines. The long level between incline Number 10 and Hollidaysburg was steep enough to allow cars to descend by gravity, with a locomotive used only to control speed.

blocks.text: National Historic Site is one of more than 380 parks in the National Park System. The National Park Service cares for these special places so that all may experience our heritage. To learn more visit www.nps.gov.

Small vertical credit line on the photograph's right edge, identifying the image source; placed after the transcriber's note per 9.5.4, at the same cell-7 indent as that note (not 4 cells further right).

print.notes: Direct worked example of 9.5.4: the transcriber's-note description of the photo and its source ('Library of Congress') are placed in a new paragraph following the (transcribed) caption text. print.printFeatures: A captioned historical photo of a locomotive with two blocks of explanatory caption text beneath it and a small vertical photo-credit line along its right edge.

resolution: A and B transcribed identical `braille.lines`, verified byte-for-byte against lines 7045-7054 after stripping the 5-character line-number field (the '(Return to Text)' line 7055 excluded). Print-content structure differed substantially: A broke this into 5 blocks (folding the right caption's sub-heading into the same block as its body text); B collapsed the whole photo/captions into 2 blocks (a heading and 2 long paragraphs) plus a separate 'other' for the photo and a separate 'source' for the credit line, which does not reflect the braille's own 6 distinct, differently-indented chunks (cell7/cell5/cell7/cell5/cell7/cell7) at all. Rebuilt from the agreed `braille.lines`' own indentation directly (not picking either run's account): 6 blocks matching the 6 physically distinct chunks, `kind:'source'` used for every cell-5/cell-7 citation-like fragment (mapped to Emboss's attribution reuse per the existing displayed-writeup.md finding F-D9). Each caption's FULL print sentence is kept in `text` (not truncated to match the braille's own ellipsis point), consistent with this whole corpus's convention (e.g. Sample 9-1) of feeding buildModel9 the complete print content and documenting the resulting over-production against the gold's own deliberately-abridged excerpt as an expected, not invented, limitation.
